Description
Unquestionably, one of the world’s most well-known silver bullion coins is the Somalia Silver Elephant. The African Wildlife Series, often known as the Zambia Silver Elephant Series, was initially released by the Bavarian State Mint in 1999. This series is one of the most varied you will find while
purchasing silver
as of 2017. Customers may now buy 1 oz. Somalia Silver Elephant Coins from
Bullion Trading LLC
‘s online and physical stores.
The African Wildlife Series Elephant Coins were first made available in 1999 by the Bavarian State Mint. The 1 oz silver coins were referred to as the Zambia Silver Elephant Series from 1999 to 2003. Although the country of issue in this series has changed, the designs’ primary focus has not. The series’ principal subject has always been the African wild elephant.
Design of Somalia 1 oz Silver Elephant Coins
The backfield of the Somalia 1 oz Silver Elephant Coin features a brand-new illustration of an African bush elephant in the wild every year.
This custom persisted when the series moved to the Somalia Silver Elephant in 2004.
The Bavarian State Mint
has continued to grow this series over the years to reach as many people as possible.
The national seal of Somalia appears on the obverse of the Somalia Silver Elephant Coin 1 oz.
The image of a crowned shield with a single star in the center, placed against a background of horizontal lines, is featured on the country’s coat of arms. Leopards flank the shield on either side, and fern leaves and cross spears are seen below.
The new Silver Elephant Coin Somalia 1 oz reverse design shows a mother bush elephant and her young offspring.
The two are seen strolling over the savanna with a few distant trees on the horizon and a small group of birds flying overhead.
Main Highlights of Somalia Silver Elephant Coin 1 oz
Contains 1 oz of .999 pure silver
Has a face value of 100 Somali Shillings.
The obverse side features the national coat of arms of Somalia.
The reverse depicts a mother elephant with its young calf on the savanna.
